holidays.name: Upsy Daisy Day
holidays.description: A cheerful unofficial observance for people who woke up on the wrong side of the bed. It encourages you to shake off the grumpies, get back up, and start the day with a smile. Think of it as a cure for the Monday-morning mood, whatever day of the week it lands on.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Its name comes from the old nursery phrase 'upsy-daisy', which people say when they lift a toddler or help someone back onto their feet.
holidays.funFact: 'Upsy-daisy' is an alteration of the older interjection 'up-a-daisy', which parents have used to cheer up stumbling toddlers for centuries.

holidays.name: National Best Friends Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the people who know your embarrassing stories and stick around anyway. Send a message, share a snack, or plan a hangout with your favorite human. Pets can be best friends too.
holidays.origin: It is an informal, unofficial observance in the United States. It is listed on June 8, and a similar friendship celebration is held on other dates.
holidays.funFact: Several different 'best friends' days appear on the calendar, so you can legitimately celebrate your favorite person more than once a year.

holidays.name: World Oceans Day
holidays.description: A global day to appreciate the sea, which covers most of our planet. People mark it with beach cleanups, aquarium visits, and pledges to cut down on single-use plastic. It reminds us that the ocean produces much of the oxygen we breathe and feeds billions of people.
holidays.origin: The idea was first proposed in 1992 at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro. The United Nations officially recognized June 8 as World Oceans Day in 2008.
holidays.funFact: Scientists estimate that more than half of the oxygen in each breath you take comes from ocean plants and plankton.
